1	# Leads
2	
3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine sends a daily (and monthly) gas nomination as a Word attachment to the HPL scheduler. Several Enron staff are copied, and someone has to re-key the volumes and confirm them back.: The same 'Calpine Daily Gas Nomination' email with 'CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc' arrives near-daily from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001. The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. - Monthly OPM (Operations Pricing Model) hours survey of activity hours by cost center: There are company-wide rollouts, reminders and Access installs. - Monthly forward curve validation: Jennifer Nguyen reviews 10 curves each month and asks the desk leads to explain the large shifts. The leads in turn ask traders and reply, often with 'the market traded higher', which leads to more follow-up questions.: The same request arrives for January, February and March, each with a list of curves and reminders. The answers barely change, and Darron notes that 'this curve will probably show up every month'. A standard commentary or automatic market-data attribution could replace this round trip. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/170.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/133.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/132.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/49.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/48.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/47.eml
- Liquidation and flash support each month: Jim Little asks the desk leads for supporting detail behind the monthly liquidation values for each region. The detail is saved by hand to an ERMS/FRED Liquidations folder, and earlier months are chased again when they are missing.: The requests say 'I WILL ALSO NEED SUPPORT FOR THE DECEMBER AND JANUARY VALUES', followed by more requests for December Denver support and for March index deals. A bad booking also forced February liquidations to be re-run. The support is gathered the same way every month. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/187.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/163.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/105.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/168.eml
- Audit and data requests handled by email: Arthur Andersen asks for monthly gas-testing items (deal ticket, confirmation, forwards detail) and sends a quarterly testing checklist for the earnings release. Ad hoc requests also come in for MTM values by counterparty and for TAGG annuity values. Desk leads forward each request on to their staff.: The requests are monthly or quarterly, the checklist matrix covers every request so far, and requests get lost or delayed ('I was on vacation... didn't see it'). The forwarding chain runs from the desk lead to an analyst. Other requests in the same vein: 'Two more counterparties need MTM values', and 'For audit purposes, can you give us a brief description' of TAGG annuities. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/120.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/118.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/91.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/90.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/89.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/137.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/136.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/6.eml
- OA (operational accounting) and flash-to-actual variances: people investigate variances between flash/CPR figures and actual Unify/GL figures, for example on the PGEV park-and-lend imbalance and physical storage inventory. Gas Accounting has started a project to collect storage book codes and inventory schedules from every desk, and Risk has collected suggestions for improving OA.: Requests include 'it is causing an OA variance for us', 'Improvement in this process will help minimize flash-to-actual variances', and 'Has any progress been made on this?'. Darron admits 'I will see a variance that is rather small and just take it without looking into the underlying cause'. The variances come back every month. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2116.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/163.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/161.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/157.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/58.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/34.eml
- Monthly manual accounting for the GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap: every month someone has to zero out the HPL sale price to GLO, update the demand-charge tickets between HPL and ENA, and book the ENA sale to EGM at the value of the crude, all before flash.: Bryce Baxter writes that 'This will require the following steps be taken monthly' and 'This needs to be done monthly prior to flash'. A follow-up in April shows the bookings were still causing confusion. It is a clear candidate for an automated rule. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml
- Weekend on-call schedulers handle pipeline events (over- and under-deliveries, cuts, confirmation changes) and then write up manual 'On Call Notes' for the team. There is also a separate weekly systems-availability on-call email.: The notes follow the same format every weekend and record phone and pager handling plus manual confirmation changes in POPS. They are recurring operational overhead. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2110.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/210.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/180.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/167.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/26.eml
- Contract administration letters and reports: Cheryl Dudley produces a twice-monthly Assignment, Termination and Expiration Report by hand, and once forgot one ('accidentally failed to do the report for March'). Termination and shut-in notification letters need several people to work out the contract terms, such as whether a contract has evergreen language and what the letter should say.: The report is periodic and distributed by hand. Contract terms are stored inconsistently: the Global Contracts system said there was no evergreen clause, but the signed confirmation had one. This leads to email back-and-forth before each letter. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2114.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2119.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2120.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2121.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/172.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/171.eml
- Imbalance and balancing work: schedulers compile lists of points where gas is owed from the RTU variance and imbalance reports, track Oasis transport imbalances, and chase meter statements to find volumes missing from nominations (the Big Cowboy/GEPL overflow 'every month for at least the past six months'). King Ranch is consistently under-nominated.: 'We have an ongoing issue every month', 'we have consistently been under nominated', and an 'Urgent' request to compile a list by hand from spreadsheets. All of this points to recurring manual reconciliation. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2126.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2127.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2128.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/170.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/160.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/159.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/166.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/191.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/190.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/189.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/183.eml
- HPL sale to AEP: transition memos keep being redistributed, deal downloads are prepared for AEP, transport contracts are sorted between ENA and HPL, and new formal procedures are being drafted (counterparty maintenance, new books, employee security, curve mapping).: The issues memo is updated and resent over and over, and new recurring request processes are being defined. This is worth checking for duplicated effort. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2104.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/212.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/206.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/187.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/156.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/155.eml
- System access, user setup and book administration done by email: requests to add users to RiskTrac or GD_NEW uploads and the Canadian script, to add a Book Admin on the website, to move books under a trading group, to supply trader website access lists, and to count monitors. Darron asks that new hires have their applications and passwords ready when they start. Renaming the Denver books would mean changing every deal by hand.: There are many small one-off access requests. Darron's feedback says new-hire setup is a recurring pain, and the book rename 'will require a great deal of time and effort to change every deal'. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/157.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/156.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/140.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/18.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/15.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/63.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/92.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/131.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/102.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/130.eml
- Origination grants and credit reserves are recorded by hand: credit sends reserve memos, traders or originators ask for origination to be granted, and mistakes have to be corrected (a $100K double grant).: Requests and corrections are routed by email to the desk lead ('Sherry Dawson said you would probably be the one to grant this origination'). One grant was made twice by mistake. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/147.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/84.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/32.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/103.eml
- Penalty charges collected by survey: settlements emails about 25 analysts asking which counterparties invoiced or netted penalties for a production month, with a same-day deadline. A desk summary is then prepared for the head trader.: Each penalty amount, counterparty and deal is collected by hand across the whole group under a deadline ('I need this information before you leave today'). This could be a standing report. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/179.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/178.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/176.eml
- Daily approval by reply email: the prelim Enovate DPR (daily position report) is sent each day 'For your approval' and approved with an 'OK' reply.: It is a recurring daily approval sent by email, and could be approved in the system or by exception only. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/161.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/155.eml
- Nomination and deal-number exchange with customers and pipelines: Equistar's monthly nominations arrive late, and the scheduler needs deal numbers from the trader to confirm them. First-of-month noms (Swift, Duke Three Rivers), flexible Katy gas lists and maintenance outages are passed along by email. Oasis is moving to online nominations.: The same information is copied by hand at each first-of-month cycle. Oasis's online nom/confirm system is an automation opportunity mentioned in the mail itself. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/152.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/144.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/153.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/158.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/201.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/200.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/150.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/149.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/202.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2130.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2108.eml
- Matching SFAS 133 hedges by hand: offsetting third-party trades have to be identified and documented for internal Transwestern/RMTC hedges, about 97 trades found by hand at year end, with the work now repeating for new trades.: The email says 'More Deals', and the effectiveness testing cannot be done without the third-party positions. A $27MM earnings impact is at stake. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/71.eml
- Recurring HR and admin collection by email: lists of potential reviewers for mid-year reviews, PBA nominations, analyst and associate needs assessments, and topic lists for training sessions are each gathered by emailing every lead.: These are periodic people-process requests gathered by hand with deadlines and reminders ('I've received only one response so far'). Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/518.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/5.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/65.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/60.eml
- Failing internal tools: the Global Standards exception-reporting Access database and the training-approval website both give errors, and the PMA files and the physical template revision are handed around by hand.: Darron writes 'I get an error when I launch the program in Access' and 'I get an error when I try to approve this'. The exception database goes unused by the gas group. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/74.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/135.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/185.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/193.eml
- Monthly gas settlements chasing price differences: settlements staff (mostly Megan Parker, also Elizabeth Hernandez and Tess Ray) email the logistics lead (Daren Farmer) one deal at a time to check prices in Sitara against counterparty invoices. Counterparties include Mirant, Texaco, DEFS, Tristar, Duke, Houston Exploration, MGI, Global Octanes and Dow (Cowtrap/Blue Dolphin).: A steady stream of single-deal questions, each needing someone to look up the trader or the trader's deal book. Requests sit unanswered (Hernandez re-sent after 3 weeks). Amounts are large (Houston Expl. $222k, MGI $10.6k), and some deals belong to traders who have left (Danny Conner). Lee Papayoti could not edit an old Enron deal after the move to AEP. Jeff,

the near future.  Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, 
we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market 
valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio.

Desk heads,

we should go to with these requests.  Also, please let these persons know 
that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several 
per week).

rules, Parties dealing in Derivatives must show third party valuations to

any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line 
"EnTelligence" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us 
to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without 
having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book.

Thanks for the help.  We'll try to get these off of your plates as soon as 
possible.

Joe

	Enron North America Corp.  From:  Bryce Baxter @ ECT                           03/05/2001 06:33 PM	
		


To:	George Weissman/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc:	Donnie Myers/NA/Enron@ENRON, Katherine Herrera/Corp/Enron@ENRON, David Baumbach/HOU/ECT@ECT 

Subject:	GLO/EGM Gas/Crude Swap

George - I've done some T-accounts (the bean counter in me) and I think the following is the best way to handle this going forward:
	
Change the existing deals, 547201 and 591307, to a zero price.  This will eliminate the A/R balance on HPL's books for GLO, but will keep the volume nom'd to GLO and will not impact UA4.
Enter a ticket on HPL for a sale to ENA for the value of the gas that was zeroed out on the above tickets.  This should be entered as a demand charge only and the amounts should be $974,144 for 1/01 and $766,304 for 2/01.
Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book purchases the demand from HPL.  The amounts would be the same as in #2 above.
Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book sells demand to EGM for the value of the crude oil for the prior month.  For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).

This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:
The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.

Once this is done, the A/R balance for GLO will be cleared, the margin will be on the ENA Wellhead book, and the intercompany transactions will move the money from EGM to HPL.  This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.  We should also know the value of the crude oil so that we can flash the sale from ENA to EGM.  If you have any questions or see a better way to do this, please let me know.  Thanks.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests (stop routing them through Risk desks)

How it is done today: The Confirmations group (Joe Hunter, Ellen Wallumrod) receives counterparty audit requests for mark-to-market values as of a past date. They have no valuation system, so they email every desk head (Gossett, Keiser, Love, Giron, Baumbach, McLaughlin); each desk head forwards to a desk person, who pulls a mini-book, exports it to Excel, blacks out Delta/Vol columns and emails it back.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/241.eml (Hunter, 02/08/2001): "Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio." ... "please let these persons know that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several per week)." ... "We do not have access to any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line \"EnTelligence\" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/240.eml: Hunter to five desk heads: "Please forward to Ellen Wallumrod the MTM valuation(mini-book) for all CoEnergy Trading Company deals as of Dec 31, 2000.  If you can export into excel and forward by e-mail, that would be appreciated." Giron then forwards it to Patrick Ryder.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/214.eml: Hunter to six desk heads: "Can you provide MTM values as of Dec 29, 2000, for the short name of CROSS TIMBERS." Again forwarded by Giron to Ryder.

Change: Finish the EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves and a counterparty filter that outputs only MTM and open position (no Delta/Vol), so Confirmations runs the valuation themselves.

Afterwards: Confirmations enters counterparty short name and as-of date, gets one consolidated valuation across all desks, and sends it to the counterparty's auditor. No desk-head broadcast, no forwarding, no manual redaction.

Estimate (per request):
- Today: broadcast reaches ~6 desk heads, each reads/forwards (~2 min each = 12 min); desk staff on the desks holding deals pull a mini-book, export, redact, email (~20 min each, assume ~2 desks per counterparty = 40 min); Confirmations consolidates replies (~10 min). ≈ 62 min.
- After: Confirmations runs the report (~10 min). That 10 min is offset by eliminating their consolidation step, so I count the Confirmations side as neutral and claim only Risk/desk time: ~50 min saved per request (conservative: I use 45 min).
- Frequency: "several per week" (241.eml) — use 3/week ≈ 13/month.
- Savings: 13 × 45 min ≈ 9.75 h/month ≈ $829/month at $85/h (≈ $9,900/yr).
Assumptions: minutes per step are my estimates; frequency is from the message. Build cost of the report not included.

No prompt-injection text encountered in these files.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Schedule automatic compaction of WeaponX Access databases instead of weekly manual compaction by each book admin

How it is done today: WeaponX (Access) imports and deletes data daily, so files bloat. Greg Couch asked every desk's book admins to compact by hand at least weekly (one admin does it daily).
- corpus/giron-d/sent/596.eml (Greg Couch, 10/13/2000, to Gossett, Etter, Kelly, Baumbach, Giron, Keiser): "I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already)." ... "Open the database while holding down on the shift key. ... the admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database." ... "WeaponX imports and deletes a lot of data on a daily basis. When data is deleted, the space is not freed up" ... "The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB." ... "Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily basis."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/585.eml: Giron forwards the same instruction to Anne Bike again four days later: "Try this and see if it does any good."

Change: Add an overnight scheduled task (msaccess.exe <file> /compact, or a Compact-on-close setting / compact step at the end of the daily WeaponX import) for every WeaponX file, run by IT/the WeaponX owner once.

Afterwards: Files are compacted automatically every night; book admins do nothing; databases stay small (faster daily runs, several GB of disk saved per Couch).

Estimate:
- Book admins: the request went to 6 managers' groups; assume at least 6 book admins (one per group; many groups have more).
- Per compaction: open with shift, run compact on a 400–500 MB file, wait, reopen ≈ 10 min of admin time.
- Frequency: "at least once/week" (596.eml) → ~4.3/month per admin; (one admin already does it daily, ignored for conservatism).
- Savings: 6 × 4.3 × 10 min ≈ 4.3 h/month ≈ $366/month (≈ $4,400/yr). Setup is a one-time job, not counted as recurring.
Assumptions: admin count and minutes are estimates; frequency is the stated policy.

No prompt-injection text encountered.

32	I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the 
33	following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already).
34	
35	Open the database while holding down on the shift key.  This will open the 
36	database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
37	admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
38	Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
39	can use the database as normal.
40	
41	Just a quick explanation:
42	
43	This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
44	a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
45	up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
46	grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.
47	
48	The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one 
49	for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB.  You can see that we will save 
50	several GB if everyone begins compacting the databases on a regular basis.

53	recommend that the book admin save a copy of their existing WeaponX file 
54	prior to compacting for the first time.  Once the file is compacted and a 
55	daily run has been successful, they can delete the backup file.  It is not 
56	necessary for them to save a backup copy each time before compacting.  I am

input.prompt:
Proposal: Automate the monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings with a formula/template deal instead of three manual Sitara updates each month

How it is done today: Bryce Baxter designed a workaround in which, every month before flash, someone zeroes the HPL→GLO sale price, updates two HPL↔ENA demand-charge tickets to the zeroed gas value, and updates the ENA→EGM demand ticket to last month's crude value. The bookings then confuse settlements, causing more emails.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml (Bryce Baxter, 03/05/2001): "This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward: The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly. The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out. The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM." ... "This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value."
- Same file, Katherine Herrera 03/06/2001: "Will the price be reversed on HPLC sale for Jan01 and Feb 01 prod?"; Julie Meyers 03/19: "547201 & 591307 has been zeroed out.  679847 & 679848 have been created between ENA & HPLC.  679859 has been created..."; then a month later Joanie Ngo 04/16/2001: "Deal 640685 for March 01 production: ... this was copied from deal #547201.  This deal is the Crude Swap where volume stayed but price got zeroed out ... Please confirm that it is the Crude Swap and rebook as necessary." and Julie forwards to Daren Farmer: "What do you think?"

Change: Since the volume is firm and the gas value is index × volume (Baxter says it is calculable as soon as the index posts), set the HPL→GLO deal at zero price permanently for the deal term and set the two HPL/ENA demand tickets as index-formula demand charges (firm volume × index) in Sitara; for the ENA→EGM leg, have the crude value entered once by the person who receives it into a single field / standard monthly template, with a deal comment flagging it as the crude swap so settlements doesn't query it.

Afterwards: The monthly work drops to one value entry (crude) instead of three ticket updates plus reconciliation questions from settlements.

Estimate (per month):
- Today: zero out the price (~5 min), calculate and update two demand tickets (~15 min), update EGM ticket (~10 min), plus the settlements query/answer loop shown in April (Ngo → Meyers → Farmer, ~3 people × 10 min = 30 min). ≈ 60 min.
- After: one crude value entry ~10 min.
- Saved ≈ 50 min/month ≈ 0.83 h ≈ $71/month (≈ $850/yr). Frequency "monthly" from 175.eml. Small but certain; the change is a one-time deal setup.

79	cc:	Donnie Myers/NA/Enron@ENRON, Katherine Herrera/Corp/Enron@ENRON, David Baumbach/HOU/ECT@ECT 
80	
81	Subject:	GLO/EGM Gas/Crude Swap
82	
83	George - I've done some T-accounts (the bean counter in me) and I think the following is the best way to handle this going forward:
84		
85	Change the existing deals, 547201 and 591307, to a zero price.  This will eliminate the A/R balance on HPL's books for GLO, but will keep the volume nom'd to GLO and will not impact UA4.
86	Enter a ticket on HPL for a sale to ENA for the value of the gas that was zeroed out on the above tickets.  This should be entered as a demand charge only and the amounts should be $974,144 for 1/01 and $766,304 for 2/01.
87	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book purchases the demand from HPL.  The amounts would be the same as in #2 above.
88	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book sells demand to EGM for the value of the crude oil for the prior month.  For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).
89	
90	This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:
91	The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
92	The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
93	The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.
94	
95	Once this is done, the A/R balance for GLO will be cleared, the margin will be on the ENA Wellhead book, and the intercompany transactions will move the money from EGM to HPL.  This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.  We should also know the value of the crude oil so that we can flash the sale from ENA to EGM.  If you have any questions or see a better way to do this, please let me know.  Thanks.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The problem is the idea, not just the evidence. More research would not change the verdict, because the mail shows the work has ended.

**Why it fails:**

1. **The work did not continue.** Baxter's 03/05/2001 note says the steps must be done "monthly as this deal goes forward." But two later emails from Megan Parker show they weren't done monthly, and that the deal stopped after May 2001:
   - `corpus/farmer-d/logistics/83.eml` (08/07/2001): Julie Meyers "completed January and February, except for one small part, but March forward was never completed." Parker then lists the bookings still needed "to finish out the transactions for March, April and May." That is a single catch-up job, not a monthly routine.
   - `corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml` (10/31/2001): the GLO deal numbers run only from Jan 01 to May 01. Parker asks about supply "for Jan through May." No deal appears after May.

   So this was a five-month episode that was cleaned up afterwards. It is not work the organization keeps doing, and a fixed monthly saving can't be claimed for it.

2. **The estimate counts a one-off as monthly.** The 30-minute settlements question-and-answer in April came up because the March deal (640685) was copied from the old Jan deal (547201) and kept its price. That happened once. It shouldn't be counted every month.

3. **The proposed change is guesswork.** Nothing in the mail shows that Sitara could book a demand charge as a formula (firm volume × index). The "one crude entry" also wouldn't stop later corrections: Parker had to correct the Jan and Feb crude values on deal 679859 after they were entered.

4. **The savings are tiny.** Even taken at face value, it is about $850 a year. In reality it was five months of a deal that has ended.

**How it could be reworked:** only by switching to a different, ongoing piece of work. For example, if the mail shows other intercompany swaps being booked by hand month after month, a proposal could be built on those. This deal can't support one.

Proposal: Standing month-end P&L audit package (top pages + curve shift reports for every book) in a shared folder that Arthur Andersen can pull, instead of monthly email requests relayed desk head → book admins → photocopies

How it is done today: Each month Arthur Andersen (Mark Austin, Sharon Smith) emails the Risk desk heads (Kelly, Keiser, Giron, Baumbach) a list of regions for "monthly testing" and asks for month-end P&L top pages, plus top pages for the five largest days and curve-shift reports. Desk heads forward to their book admins, who pull and print/photocopy the reports; AA then chases missing items and asks who is responsible for each desk.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/317.eml (Austin, 01/16/2001, to Kelly, Keiser, Giron, Baumbach): "As part of our monthly testing we review the monthly Natural Gas P & L Statement and identify specific regions for which we would like to review additional documentation. ... We are requesting that you supply the P & L top pages for the last day of the month for those regions that are applicable to you." Austin then chases: "Is there someone else that can direct us to?  I would like to get this information as soon as it is possible." Giron forwards to Walker, Wolfe, Bagwell: "Could you please read this request and get back to Mark with the info ASAP?" and again to Kam Keiser.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/516.eml (Sharon Smith, 11/06/2000): "In order for us to complete our monthly gas testing, please provide the following items. P&L top sheet for the last day of August.  Additionally, if the majority of the P&L pertains to curve shift, please provide the P&L top pages for five of  the  largest days including the Curve Shift Reports." Giron to four staff: "Please get this info to me and I will pass it on to AA."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/420.eml (Smith, 12/06/2000): "In review of our third quarter file, we have not received the P&L top pages or curve shift reports for the following regions:  West Firm, FT Northwest and Mgmt. West." Giron: "Pull this together and then call Sharon so they can come get the copies."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/299.eml (Austin, 01/24/2001): "please direct me to the individual responsible for each of the desks listed below.  As part of my testing, I will be looking to identify the P&L drivers for each month as well as the days throughout the month that have the largest P&L."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/120.eml (Austin, 03/14 & 03/27/2001): "As part of our monthly gas testing, could you please provide the deal ticket, confirmation, and forwards detail for Deal #QT5176" then "Could you please let me know the status on this information as soon as possible?"

Change: At month-end close, have the P&L system (or a book-admin macro run once) save PDF/print files of each book's month-end top page, daily top pages and curve-shift reports into a read-only audit folder, with a one-page index of book → responsible book admin. Give AA read access. Origination deal tickets/confirms stay on request.

Afterwards: AA picks the regions and the five largest days straight from the folder; no broadcast, forwarding, photocopies, chase emails, or "who is responsible" questions. Desk staff only take the driver-discussion call (unchanged).

Estimate (per month, Risk side only; AA's time not counted):
- Today: 3–4 desk heads each read/forward/collect/hand off (~15 min each ≈ 50 min); 3–4 book admins per desk head's group pull, print, copy several regions incl. five largest days and curve-shift reports (~20 min each, ~8 admins across the groups ≈ 160 min); chases/missing items (e.g. 420.eml quarter-end close-out) ~20 min. ≈ 230 min.
- After: saving to the folder is automated; a book admin spot-checks the folder at close (~20 min total).
- Saved ≈ 210 min ≈ 3.5 h/month ≈ $298/month (≈ $3,570/yr). Frequency "monthly testing" stated in 317.eml, 516.eml, 120.eml.

- After: saving to the folder is automated; a book admin spot-checks the folder at close (~20 min total).
- Saved ≈ 210 min ≈ 3.5 h/month ≈ $298/month (≈ $3,570/yr). Frequency "monthly testing" stated in 317.eml, 516.eml, 120.eml.
Minutes are my estimates.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal as a duplicate. Nothing is wrong with the idea or the evidence. Another critic has already saved the same work as "Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests" in `decisions.md`. It proposes the same change: a read-only report for Confirmations that values a counterparty's deals across all desks as of a past date. It also cites the same messages: giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240 and 241.

**What I checked before rejecting:**
- Your quotes are accurate. 241.eml does say Confirmations has no valuation system, gets "several per week" requests, and wants EnTelligence so it no longer needs a Risk person or has to black out Delta/Vol. In 240.eml and 214.eml, Hunter's request goes to the desk heads and Giron forwards it to Patrick Ryder.
- I found one more occurrence. In 137.eml, Gossett sends five desk heads another request for two more counterparties. In 136.eml, Carole Frank sends the West desk totals back about an hour after the request reached the desk.
- Your estimate is reasonable. That is 45 minutes of desk time per request, at 3 a week (13 a month), which `check` computed as 9.75 hours, or $829 a month. 3 a week is a fair reading of "several per week."

**Something the managers may want to look at:** the saved version claims $1,694 a month, about twice your figure, from the same evidence. So it assumes about 90 minutes per request (or about twice as many requests). That may be too high, but changing it would mean reviewing the saved item. Resubmitting this proposal won't do it.

No more research would change the verdict, because the duplication is the only problem. I've recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`.

- audit-mtm-valuations.json (the rewritten proposal, with 137 and 136 added)
- audit-mtm-valuations-reject.json (the recorded rejection)

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is entry 2 in `decisions.md`, at 10 minutes × 26 times a month = 4.33 hours, or about $368 a month.

**What checks out.** Both cited messages say what the proposal claims:
- Greg Couch asked "each of your book admins using WeaponX" to compact their files "at least once/week". His message went to six managers.
- He gives the manual steps: open the file holding the shift key, then run Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database.
- He explains why the files grow: data is imported and deleted every day, and Access does not free the space.
- The 520→30 MB and 400→12 MB figures are his, and so is the note that Crystal already compacts daily.

No other critic had saved or rejected this work in `decisions.md`.

**What I changed before saving:**
- **Who sent the mail.** Both files are Darron Giron forwarding Couch's 10/13/2000 message to Anne Bike, on 10/13 and again on 10/17. They are not Couch's own sent mail. I quote the embedded text, which is accurate.
- **Unsupported claims removed.** "Faster daily runs" appears nowhere in the mail, so I took it out. I also dropped the "several GB of disk saved" benefit. Couch credits that space to regular compaction of any kind, so doing it by hand saves the same space and the change itself does not.
- **How often.** I recorded the rate as 6 a week: one compaction per admin per week, with one admin per manager's group, so six admins. The number six is an inference from the six recipients; the mail does not give it. It is probably low, since Couch writes "book admins" in the plural and one admin compacts daily.
- **Minutes.** I kept 10 minutes per compaction, counting the wait while a file of several hundred MB compacts. This is an estimate; the mail says nothing about duration.

**Remaining weakness.** The mail only shows the instruction being given and forwarded. It does not show admins actually doing it week after week. The savings rest on the instruction being followed as written.

Proposal: Book ECC (Enron Canada) master-swap counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically at entry, instead of monthly book-by-book searches and manual "flips"

Please check decisions.md first; I don't see this saved or rejected.

How it is done today: Deals with counterparties that have master swap agreements with ECC (Aquila Canada, Duke Energy Marketing, Engage, etc.) keep landing in Houston books (FT-West, MGMT-WEST, FT-Ontario, NG-EXOTIC…) as settling with ENA. Before each month's Canadian invoicing, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary) searches TAGG, emails 5–7 Risk desk heads lists of deal IDs and asks them to search all their books; each desk head forwards to several book admins who search and flip; late finds force re-runs of liquidations and miss invoices. An automatic EOL booking rule exists for TransCanada and Dynegy Canada but not for others.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/292.eml (Vallejo 01/26/2001, to Gossett, Giron, Kelly, Keiser, Johnson, Guggenheim; Giron forwards to 5 staff "Please flip these if applicable."): "Here is a list of deals that I know of that need to be flipped to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book right away.  Please go through your books to see if there are any deals that I might have missed." ... "I've spoken to Jennifer Denny with EOL about getting a program set up for Duke deals similar to ones we have with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC, but I don't think this has happened yet."

1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only report that values a counterparty's deals across all desks as of a past date, so Risk analysts no longer do it by hand. ($1,694.05 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/136.eml, giron-d/sent/137.eml, giron-d/sent/214.eml, giron-d/sent/240.eml, giron-d/sent/241.eml
4	2. Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases: Compact every WeaponX file automatically each night so book admins no longer do it by hand. ($368.05 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/585.eml, giron-d/sent/596.eml
5	3. Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Book Canadian-settled deals straight into FT-US/CAND-ERMS, and send each book owner a nightly list of any that land elsewhere, instead of a monthly manual search of every Houston book. ($298.35 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/108.eml, giron-d/sent/114.eml, giron-d/sent/195.eml, giron-d/sent/270.eml, giron-d/sent/292.eml, giron-d/sent/360.eml, giron-d/sent/539.eml, giron-d/sent/550.eml
6	4. Monthly roll of Sitara transport usage tickets: A month-end job extends each active usage ticket, fills its rate from the matrix/Unify rates and carries last month's volume, leaving people only an exception list. ($198.05 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml, farmer-d/logistics/867.eml
7	
8	# Rejected
9	
10	- Calpine daily gas nomination by emailed Word document: Have Calpine send its daily nomination through a structured feed or web form that loads into scheduling, and confirm only when volumes change.. Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. The re-keying, the daily phone call and the 'no change' confirmation that make up most of the 10 minutes are not shown; the confirmation rests on one undated message that does not match the rest of the archive. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
11	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill managers' monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys from ATEs/SAP and system reports so managers only correct exceptions.. Why: The organization had already built most of this: from late 2000 the Access hours survey carries forward commercial teams and FTEs and shows prior-month hours, and the driver survey already let groups send a standard report instead. The proposal mistakes a one-off January 2001 SAP glitch for the normal monthly process, and hours by activity cannot be taken from ATEs/SAP. Research that could settle it: Find what managers still do by hand each month in the Access tool after the January 2001 SAP changeover (for example, splitting hours by activity and team, as in 84.eml), how long it takes, and whether any driver surveys were still sent after August 2000; then size only that remaining work.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
14	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
15	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry.. Why: The swap covered only January to May 2001 and its bookings were done as a one-time cleanup months later, not as monthly work, so there is no ongoing work for the change to save.
16	- Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests: Finish EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios without routing requests through the Risk desks.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
17	- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
18	- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
19	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
20	- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
21	- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240, 241, plus 136).
22	- Weekly manual compact of WeaponX databases: Compact each desk's WeaponX file automatically every night instead of having each book admin do it by hand every week.. Why: The same work and change is already saved in decisions.md as item 2, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml).
23	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Block known wrong-entity counterparties at TAGG deal entry with a credit-kept 'use instead' mapping, and route each Credit Report row to the owning book administrator.. Why: The 65 minutes a day rests on a 'fixed mapping' that the mail contradicts (the Aquila/Utilicorp rebook runs in opposite directions, the Louis Dreyfus target changes, and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself), on a repeat rate of half when the cited reports show about a third, and on six desk heads forwarding every day when only Giron's forwards, often sent days late in batches, appear in the mail. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs that always have the same target. Find mail from book administrators or Confirmations, such as Julie Brewer's chase in 124.eml, that shows who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Check whether desk heads other than Giron forward the report at all, given that the book administrators are already on its distribution list.

Proposal: Route the daily Credit Report rebooks straight to the owning book admin (by TAGG book), and check counterparty legal entity at deal entry, instead of a 33-person broadcast that each desk lead forwards by hand

Please check decisions.md first; I don't see this saved or rejected.

How it is done today: Every business day Credit (Russell Diamond / Veronica Espinoza) emails a "Credit Report" to ~33 people (Confirmations, Calgary, Credit, and the Risk desk heads Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach, McLaughlin, Giron, Love). It lists counterparty, TAGG# and action ("Rebook to …" the correct legal entity, or "Pending <credit officer>"). It does not say which book the deal is in. Each desk head forwards it to a book admin, who scans the whole list for deals in their books and rebooks them in TAGG.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/263.eml (Giron forwards Diamond's "Credit Report - 1/30/01" to Carole Frank on 02/02/2001, three days late). The list has ~30 lines, e.g. "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings  qO0682.1  Rebook to Louis Dreyfus Corporation", "Southern Company Energy Marketing  qO3294.1.2  Rebook to Mirant Americas Energy Marketing LP", "Unocal Corporation    qO1049.1  Rebook to Union Oil Company of California", "Bank of America N.A.    qO2878.1.2  Rebook to Bank of America, National Association".
- corpus/giron-d/sent/14.eml (Giron forwards "Credit Report - 5/7/01" to Carole Frank): "CMS Energy Corporation  v78462.1,v78468.1 Rebook to CMS Marketing, Services and Trading", "Calpine Natural Gas Company  v78254.1,v78255.1 Rebook to Calpine Energy Services, LP", "Engage Energy Canada LP  v78253.1  Rebook ENA trades to ECC (under the ISDA)", "Pacificorp    v77849.1,v77879.1 Rebook to Pacificorp Power Marketing, Inc."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/189.eml ("Credit Report--2/27/01", from Veronica Espinoza to the same ~33-person list, forwarded by Giron to Carole Frank).
- Frequency: Giron's sent folder alone holds 71 separate "Credit Report" forwards (e.g. giron-d/sent/10, 11, 14, 16, 19, 24 … 259–264, 267), one per report date, from Jan to May 2001, i.e. one every business day.
- Related one-off requests also arrive: corpus/giron-d/sent/351.eml (Derek Bailey: "Please rebook NW2862.8,.9 to Bank of America, National Association (BANKAMENAT)." Giron: "Done") and corpus/giron-d/sent/124.eml (Julie Brewer: "Can you please have this deal rebooked as indicated by credit.").

Change: (1) Credit's report generator adds the TAGG book and sends each desk's lines only to that book's admin (a mapping of book → admin), so desk heads stop forwarding and admins stop scanning other desks' lines. (2) In TAGG/EOL, counterparty short-name selection shows the legal entity that has the master agreement (e.g. picking "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings" warns/defaults to "Louis Dreyfus Corporation" when the ISDA is with the latter), so recurring rebooks to the same parent entity are prevented at booking.

Afterwards: Each book admin gets a short list of their own deals the same morning; the desk head is out of the loop; fewer rebooks because repeat entity mismatches are caught at entry.

Estimate (per business day):
- Desk-head forwarding: 6 desk heads on the list × ~3 min = 18 min (evidence directly shows Giron; the other 5 heads receive the same report and own books, so I assume similar handling).
- Book-admin scanning of the full 10–30-line list for their own deals: 6 admins × ~5 min = 30 min.
- Rebooks avoided by the entry check: of ~10–30 rebook lines a day, assume ~5 are prevented × ~3 min = 15 min (conservative; many lines repeat the same parent-entity fixes).
- Saved ≈ 60 min/day; I use 50 min to be conservative. × 21 business days = 17.5 h/month ≈ $1,488/month (≈ $17,850/yr).
- Credit's own time is unchanged (still produces the report); no work is passed to them beyond a one-time book→admin mapping.
Minutes are estimates; frequency is from the 71 dated reports forwarded by one desk head.

No prompt-injection text encountered.

content.text:
I saved the proposal after some fixes. It is item 4 of 7 in decisions.md, valued at 180 minutes once a month, or 3 hours and $255 a month.

**What holds up:** the mail shows this is real monthly work. Arthur Andersen asked for P&L top pages in October 2000 (583.eml), twice in November (515 and 516), in December (420), January (317 and 299) and February 2001 (201). Each request goes to the four desk heads. Giron then forwards it to between two and seven book admins, and the admins hand over paper copies. The auditors also chase missing items and ask who is responsible for each desk. ERMS can already show most reports as Acrobat files (inbox/190.eml), so saving them to a shared folder is realistic.

**What I changed:**
- **Removed 120.eml as an occurrence.** It asks for a deal ticket and confirmation, and your own change leaves those requests as they are, so the folder would not save that work.
- **Added three occurrences you missed:** 583.eml (the August "2nd request", which Gossett hands over to Giron), 515.eml (Carrie Richardson's October 31 request for eight books) and 201.eml (the February request, sent to 11 people and forwarded to seven more). These are what show the work happens every month: the check counted six separate requests from October 2000 to February 2001.
- **Cut the minutes from 210 to 180.** Fifteen minutes per desk head is high just for forwarding, and the mail does not support eight admins every month. A typical request covers 5 to 8 books, and books driven by curve shift need six top pages plus curve shift reports. That works out to about 20 minutes per book (around 140 minutes), plus about 40 minutes for the desk heads and some chasing, minus about 20 minutes to check the folder afterwards. These minutes are estimates; the mail doesn't say how long the work takes.
- **Added a practical caveat.** The auditors lost access to Enron's Lotus Notes after February 28 (201.eml), so they may need a copy of the folder rather than direct read access.
- **Added two stalls:** in 317.eml the auditors' work waits because Giron is travelling, and in 420.eml they cannot close their third-quarter file until the missing reports arrive.

No other critic had saved or rejected the same work.

The saved proposal is at C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\aa-monthly-pl-top-pages.json

Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. 14	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.

16	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
17	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
18	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry.. Why: The swap covered only January to May 2001 and its bookings were done as a one-time cleanup months later, not as monthly work, so there is no ongoing work for the change to save.
19	- Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests: Finish EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios without routing requests through the Risk desks.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
20	- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
21	- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
22	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
23	- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
24	- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240, 241, plus 136).
25	- Weekly manual compact of WeaponX databases: Compact each desk's WeaponX file automatically every night instead of having each book admin do it by hand every week.. Why: The same work and change is already saved in decisions.md as item 2, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml).
26	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Block known wrong-entity counterparties at TAGG deal entry with a credit-kept 'use instead' mapping, and route each Credit Report row to the owning book administrator.. Why: The 65 minutes a day rests on a 'fixed mapping' that the mail contradicts (the Aquila/Utilicorp rebook runs in opposite directions, the Louis Dreyfus target changes, and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself), on a repeat rate of half when the cited reports show about a third, and on six desk heads forwarding every day when only Giron's forwards, often sent days late in batches, appear in the mail. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs that always have the same target. Find mail from book administrators or Confirmations, such as Julie Brewer's chase in 124.eml, that shows who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Check whether desk heads other than Giron forward the report at all, given that the book administrators are already on its distribution list.
27	- Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX databases: Have WeaponX compact itself automatically (scheduled overnight compact or Compact on Close) so book admins stop doing it by hand.. Why: The same work, citing the same two messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases'.
28	- Monthly search and flip of ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Auto-book ECC master-swap counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS at entry (EOL rule plus TAGG default) and send a nightly exception list to book owners.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/108, 114, 270, 292, 360).
29	- Rebooking deals to the right legal entity from the daily Credit Report: Add a credit-maintained alias table in TAGG that books known wrong entities to the approved one, and route each day's remaining exceptions by book instead of a desk lead forwarding the whole report. Why: The mail contradicts the fixed wrong-to-right pairs the alias table depends on (the same entity is sent to different targets, and Aquila/Utilicorp are rebooked in both directions), and the 9 minutes a day of West-desk rebooks, which make up half the savings, are not supported by anything in the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk's books and how long a rebook takes, and check across all the reports whether each wrong entity always goes to the same target (only about 10 of the ~70 forwarded reports have the list in the message body).
30	- Recurring alias-to-entity rebooks from the daily Credit Report: Credit and Global Counterparty keep an alias table that TAGG/EOL deal entry uses to default or block the legal entity, so repeat rebooks are never created.. Why: No mail shows who does the rebooks, how long each one takes, or that about 3 repeat lines a day belong to any one desk. The mappings are not fixed either: Aquila is rebooked to Utilicorp United on 1/30/01 (263.eml) but Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management on 3/19/01 (149.eml), and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is 'rebooked' to itself (149.eml). So 15 minutes a day is a guess. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs whose target never changes. Then find mail from book admins or Confirmations (for example Julie Brewer's 'Rebooks' request in 124.eml) showing who rebooks, how long a rebook takes and which lines are the West desk's.

Each month at Seven Oaks, TECO (PG&E) makes an adjustment to the allocation 
to either pay HPLC for underages or charge HPLC for overtakes - ie. the 
difference between what our producers put in the plant and what we take from 
the plant after shrinkage.  This adjustment arrangement doesn't seem to be 
papered - it's just occurred each month for the past 5 years on a relatively 
routine basis.

Since the adjustment arrangement isn't papered, we've been having difficulty 
properly reflecting the deal in sitara and unify.  It has been suggested that 
we try to paper the deal for posterity (the lease to TECO has 9 more years to 
run), but, in view of the forthcoming expiration of the primary term of both 
the Comstock and Oryx (Sun and/or Kerr-McGee) contracts, I'm reluctant to 
open this can of worms.  I'd like your thoughts.

George x3-6992

165	- Flows with no deal in Sitara, or with expired contracts or deals: settlements cannot pay or invoice until someone creates, extends or releases the deal. content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded it in `decisions.md`. You said it wasn't there, but it is, in two places. Some of it is already saved, and the rest has been rejected three or four times before.

**Already saved.** The desk-head forwarding part is item 7 in `decisions.md`, "Forwarding the daily Credit Report to a book admin" ($24.65 a month). It cites the same 71 forwards from Giron's sent folder that this proposal uses for its frequency. So the 18 minutes a day for forwarding is that same work again.

**The rest repeats claims rejected before.** Rejections 22, 26, 29 and 30 in `decisions.md` cover the same two ideas:

- **Six desk heads × 3 min forwarding, and six admins × 5 min scanning (48 of the 60 minutes).** Only Giron's forwards appear in the mail, all to Carole Frank, and they are often days late. For example, 263.eml forwards the 1/30/01 report on 2/2/01. No mail shows Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach, McLaughlin or Love forwarding the report. No mail shows any admin scanning the list for their own deals or how long that takes. Several people who rebook are already on the distribution list, including Derek Bailey (351.eml) and Julie Brewer (14.eml), so routing by book would save them little.
- **The entry check (15 min a day).** The check needs a fixed "wrong entity → right entity" mapping, and the mail contradicts that. Aquila is rebooked to Utilicorp United on 1/30/01 (263.eml), but Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management on 3/19/01 (149.eml). The Louis Dreyfus target changes between reports. In 149.eml, AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself. "~5 prevented a day" also assumes these lines belong to one set of desks and that half of them repeat. Earlier reviews found about a third repeat, and nothing in the mail shows which desk's books they are in.

**Idea or evidence.** Reaching the admin directly is already saved. The entry check is a reasonable idea, but the evidence for it is missing and partly contradicts it. More research could settle it:

1. Find mail from desk heads other than Giron, or from book admins or Confirmations, showing them forwarding the report, picking out their own lines, or rebooking, and how long that takes.
2. Count rebook lines across all 71 reports and keep only the counterparty pairs whose target never changes. Size the entry check on that count alone.

I didn't run `check`, because the duplicate and the earlier rejections decided it.

Rejection file: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\credit-report-routing-reject.json`
